subject: Next steps: deployment path & audit artifacts for PHI use
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Tom Blake <tom.blake@medicahealth.com>
Date: Sat, 11 Apr 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: deployment options & compliance artifacts (PHI use)

Hi Elena —

Thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and proposed next steps so your audit team has visibility.

Summary of what we heard on the call:
- You expect to send PHI to the model for clinical summarization (transcriptions + brief notes).
- Security needs: BAA/HIPAA coverage, SOC 2 Type II evidence, and demonstrable audit logs for any access to PHI.
- Preference to avoid on-prem unless required; primary evaluation is between Redwood Hosted API (with BAA) vs Dedicated GPU pools vs Private VPC.

High-level mapping (tradeoffs):
- Hosted API + BAA: Fastest to production, Redwood-managed infrastructure, BAA available, encryption in transit + at rest, limited network isolation. Good if you can rely on our managed controls and SOC 2 scope.
- Dedicated (reserved capacity): Same Redwood control plane but dedicated GPU capacity, stronger tenancy/segmentation, lower multitenant blast radius; typically used when procurement wants dedicated resources and more SLA/throughput predictability.
- Private VPC / On-prem: Strongest isolation and customer-controlled networking/KMS; required when internal auditors mandate host/network-level control or for air-gapped workflows. Longer lead times and additional ops responsibilities.

Requested artifacts (we will share):
- SOC 2 Type II summary + control matrix (redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf)
- HIPAA/BAA template and scope (hipaa-baa-template-v2.docx)
- Audit artifact checklist (audit-artifact-checklist.xlsx) — items we can produce on request (audit logs, key rotation records, penetration test reports, uptime reports).

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll send the SOC 2 summary, draft BAA, and the checklist (attached).
2) Introduce our security engineer (Jonas) and SE (Aditya) to your security team for a focused session on technical controls and evidence mapping — can we target next Wed 4/14?
3) If your auditors require private hosting, we’ll scope effort/cost and provide an estimated timeline for Private VPC or on-prem deployment.

If you want an immediate cost delta for Dedicated vs Hosted, we can include an order-of-magnitude in the follow-up.

Best,

Marissa Cole
Senior Account Exec | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0194

Attachments: redwood-soc2-summary-2025.pdf; hipaa-baa-template-v2.docx; audit-artifact-checklist.xlsx

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the clear recap and for sending the artifacts. A couple quick clarifications from our side:
- Our internal auditors will want to know if PHI is ever persisted beyond short-term KV cache (for model context). Can you confirm retention policy and options for zero-retention?
- SOC 2: we need to confirm the scope (is inference/eval pipeline included?). Please highlight any exclusions.
- If we go Dedicated, will we still get audit logs with the same fidelity (per-request traces, token-level cost breakdowns)?

Also: there’s a strong preference from procurement to see a cost delta (monthly) between Hosted w/ BAA and Dedicated reserved capacity to present to finance. Can you include a ballpark?

I’ll check with our security lead (cc: security@medicahealth.com) about availability for a call next week.

Thanks —
Elena
Director, Product Operations | MedicaHealth

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@medicahealth.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>, Tom Blake <tom.blake@medicahealth.com>
Date: Mon, 13 Apr 2026 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment options & compliance artifacts (PHI use)

Great questions — looping in Aditya (SE) and Jonas (Security) to provide the technical/ops details below and to join the call.

Answers at a high level (we’ll expand on the call):
- Retention and PHI: By default our runtime keeps short-lived KV cache that is ephemeral for inference sessions; we can configure zero-persistence modes where nothing is written to long-term storage. For customers routing PHI, we typically recommend Private VPC or Dedicated with strict isolation + customer-managed KMS if policy requires it.
- SOC 2 scope: our latest SOC 2 Type II report covers core production services (control plane, runtime, storage subsystems used by hosted and dedicated offerings). The report includes auditing around access controls, encryption, and change management — I’ve highlighted scope exclusions in the attached PDF.
- Audit logs in Dedicated: yes, Dedicated provides the same per-request tracing and token/latency breakdowns, plus an option to export logs to your SIEM (via secure forwarding).

Ballpark cost: Hosted + BAA (month): estimate $6k–$12k depending on ingest and tokens. Dedicated (reserved) starting commit: $45k/mo for a small dedicated pool (includes baseline throughput and 24/7 SLA) — final pricing depends on required RPS and model family. We’ll put a more precise estimate in the proposal.

Aditya / Jonas — can you confirm the KMS options and the specific audit artifacts we can provide for evidence (I listed items in the checklist but please expand)? Also, please propose two 45-min slots for Wed/Thu next week for the security deep-dive.

Thanks,
Marissa

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: deployment options & compliance artifacts (PHI use)

Hi all — quick technical note and inventory of artifacts we can provide for your auditors.

KMS & encryption:
- Hosted/Dedicated: We support provider-managed KMS (default) and customer-managed keys via AWS KMS / GCP KMS / Azure Key Vault for encryption-at-rest. Customer-managed KMS gives you key rotation and centralized control.
- Private VPC / On-prem: Customer retains full control of keys and can enforce HSM-backed KMS.

Retention & data flow:
- Inference path: request -> runtime (ephemeral KV cache, configurable TTL) -> optional long-term storage (disabled by default for PHI workflows). We can enable zero-retention where artifacts are not persisted beyond request lifecycle.

Audit artifacts we can produce (examples):
- SOC 2 Type II report (summary + full report under NDA)
- Control mapping spreadsheet (which control covers which artifact)
- Access logs with per-request IDs (exportable to S3/Cloud Storage with time-bounded retention)
- Key rotation logs (for customer-managed KMS)
- Pen test engagement report (redacted)
- Runtime config snapshots (shows isolation settings, network policies)

Attachments I’m including here: audit-artifact-checklist.xlsx (detailed list), and a short KMS decision matrix PDF.

Availability: Wed 2026-04-14 10:30–11:15 PT or Thu 2026-04-15 09:00–09:45 PT work for me — please pick a slot and I’ll send calendar invites.

—Jonas
